title: Toward Subspace-Perturbed Trajectory-Aware Backdoor Attacks in Deep Reinforcement Learning
claim: A unified attack framework combines three coordinated modules, each handling one decision, to achieve stealthy, efficient and value-consistent poisoning.
layout: Top scenario banner, three colored module panels below, dashed arrows converging on bottom label
description: A wide figure with a gray banner on top showing the outer-loop attack scenario. Icons run left to right: agent, environment, replay buffer, attacker and backdoored policy. Arrows are labeled Interaction and Trajectory, and a dashed box marks offline data poisoning. Below are three colored panels, each opened by an arrow from the banner. The blue panel, Where to Inject, shows Atari frames, a 3D variance-subspace surface with benign and triggered points, and the equation s† = s + ε·u_d. The green panel, When to Poison, shows a trajectory curve, then a funnel narrowing from all steps to top-m candidates to final-K steps, with RTG and TD-error formulas. The yellow panel, How to Reward, shows the reward decomposition r†_t as a sum of kernel, coefficient and suppression terms, plus a state-transition diagram with ±Δr arrows. Each panel ends in a banner: Stealth Trigger, Optimal Poisoning Set and Bounded Deviation. Dashed arrows join them at Three-Module Parallel Structure.
caption: Overview of the SpecDRL Framework. The framework orchestrates three coordinated modules to achieve high poisoning
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning agents are in- creasingly used in safety-critical domains but remain vulnerable to stealthy backdoor attacks. Existing outer-loop attacks face a trade-off be- tween perceptual stealth, poisoning efficiency, and value-function consistency, often making the at- tack ineffective or easily exposed. To address these challenges, we propose SpecDRL, a uni- fied framework that ❶ embeds triggers in the least sensitive subspaces of the state manifold via Subspace-Aware Injection, exploiting percep- tual blind spots, ❷ selects the most influential time steps for poisoning through Value-Guided Strategic Sampling based on Return-to-Go and Temporal-Difference error, and ❸ preserves re- ward integrity via Bellman-Consistent Dynamic Reward Poisoning, which analytically enforces ϵ- consistency of value functions and bounds global return deviations. Experiments across 12 Atari en- vironments demonstrate that SpecDRL achieves near-100% attack success, accelerates backdoor convergence, and maintains benign task perfor- mance.
